components.name: Sourced route sketch
components.description: Known coordinates appear as numbered points in visiting order. At least two located stops are needed; the caption discloses partial coverage.

narrative.overview: A quiet navy canvas, a lilac comparison plot and a browsable collection whose evidence remains close at hand. Prospector, Job Scout, Recruiter and Day Tripper share this report system. Day Tripper adds a bounded ordered itinerary and a sourced coordinate route sketch. Hierarchy comes from typography, spacing and selection; unknown evidence remains visible in the chart and assessment.
keyCharacteristics: Dark tonal surfaces with one lilac selection accent.
A readable radar paired with bounded, browsable results.
Plain labels, visible source evidence and tabular scores.
Keyboard access, reduced motion and a light print treatment.
An ordered itinerary and schematic route preserve coordinate provenance and coverage.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Use color to support an explicit label. Unknown scores are written as Unknown and leave gaps in the radar.

rules.name: The Plain Heading Rule
rules.body: Lead with a concise title. Add supporting text when it explains evidence, scope or a recovery action.

dos: Do keep selected state, evidence coverage and unknown facts distinguishable in text as well as color.
Do preserve bounded scrolling and incremental result loading.
Do keep the offline report self-contained, including its font and interaction code.
Do provide a visible focus outline and honor reduced motion.
Do keep source evidence available beside its assessment.
Do limit an itinerary to one to five distinct saved stops.
Do preserve original stop numbers, coordinate source links and located-stop coverage.
Do stack itinerary stops above the route on mobile and give mobile sort its own full-width row.
Do keep individual stops and route figures intact in print.
donts: Do not turn unknown values into zero scores or close their radar gaps.
Do not add shadows, excessive cards or decorative accents that weaken the tonal hierarchy.
Do not let result histories or evidence excerpts grow the page without bounds.
Do not add repetitive supporting copy beneath every heading.
Do not hide a capped radar population behind a claim that every result is plotted.
Do not invent missing coordinates or present the schematic as street routing or verified travel times.
